# 0016 — the download reports its own quality, and parking gained a reason

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2026-09-10
- Answers [#23](https://github.com/Bamo16/crateside/issues/23).
- Settles what [ADR 0015](0015-hold-is-removed-and-the-playlist-is-the-way-out.md) deliberately
  left open when it ruled hold out as the mechanism for this.

## Context

crateside predicted audio quality from the YouTube API: `PremiumOutlookReader` looked for the
*Auto-generated by YouTube* marker in a video's description and inferred that anything without it
was an ordinary upload. The marker is precise when it fires and says nothing when it does not —
of 226 corpus videos without it, 94 (42%) were premium anyway (`docs/premium-outlook.md`).

Meanwhile `stemforge-cli download --json` has been reporting `isPremium`, `premiumShortfall` and
`premiumStatus` on every download, and `EvidenceRunner.DownloadOutput` deserialized `succeeded`,
`path` and `error` and dropped the rest. StemForge's own comment says the fields exist so that
*"those who care about acquisition quality can assert it per input rather than reading provenance
tags off the finished file"*.

So the guess and the measurement were both available, and crateside was using the guess.

## Decision

**The trigger is the measured outcome, and only the part of it about the upload.**
`premiumShortfall` is too blunt — it is true for all four non-ideal outcomes. `premiumStatus`
carries the name, and StemForge's `PremiumStatus` separates them because each calls for a
different response:

| status | what crateside does |
|---|---|
| `NoPremiumLadder` | parks the track — a song version may exist |
| `SourceHasNoPremiumAudio` | parks the track — a property of the upload |
| `NotSignedIn` | nothing |
| `AccountNotPremium` | nothing |
| `PremiumNotSelected` | nothing; crateside pins no format, so its downloads never land here |
| `Premium`, `NotApplicable` | nothing |

The two session outcomes are true of *every* download at once. Stopping one track at a time for
them would be the wrong shape of alarm, and swapping that track's source would fix nothing.
Whether they deserve a surface of their own is still open; this does not answer it by accident,
and the outcome is recorded either way so that the question can be answered later from data.

**It stops before the verdict, and that is correctness rather than thrift.** A swap copies the
verdict forward ([keytag ADR 0008](../../../keytag/docs/adr/0008-a-restatement-is-not-a-run.md)),
so a key derived from poor audio would be *restated* onto the better upload rather than
re-derived, and nothing would tell the user to force a re-judge. Blocking the verdict blocks
separation for free: `QueueView.AwaitingSeparation` is built from tracks that have a verdict.

Detection still runs. It is deterministic, contends for nothing, and the user may well resolve the
finding by saying the audio is fine — in which case the evidence is already in hand and the track
moves on without re-detecting.

**The finding lives in the working set, beside the audio it describes.** Not in `queue.json` with
the user's standing instructions, and not in the job store. It is a fact about *this download*, so
it must die exactly when the download does: a swap discards the working set, the replacement is
fetched, and the answer is measured again rather than inherited.

**The user's acceptance lives there too, for the same reason.** "Use it anyway" is a statement
about the audio on disk, not a standing instruction about the track. Keeping it beside the
measurement means a later swap cannot silently inherit it — a stale acceptance would let a second
poor upload through without ever showing the user a finding. That co-location is a deliberate
exception to [ADR 0014](0014-the-song-is-the-identity-and-the-name-is-not.md)'s separation of what
the user owns from what was derived: the principle there is that a user's statement must not be
overwritten by a derivation, and nothing here overwrites it. What settles it is lifetime, and
these two have exactly the same one.

**`TrackState.Parked` gained a reason rather than a sibling state.** `Parked` already meant
"crateside stopped, your turn", which is exactly what this is. The chip already had a reason slot,
`TrackFilter.NeedsAttention` and the group-0 ordering already caught `Parked`, and a second state
would have needed new arms in all of them while still meaning the same thing. `ParkReason` names
the axis that actually differs: what resolving it takes.

`CanChangePlan` now gates on `ParkReason.NoKey` specifically. It used to read "parked" as "the GPU
has already run, so the recipe is fixed", which is true of want-of-a-key and false of a shortfall —
a track parked over its download has had nothing separated and is still open to a different recipe.

## Consequences

**The predicted advisory is gone.** `PremiumOutlookReader.AdvisoryFor` and `WorkOrder.Advisory`
were tested and rendered nowhere; the measured outcome is what the row says now. `PremiumOutlook`
itself stays — its one live use, routing an art track to its `music.youtube.com` URL in
`WorkOrder.Compose`, is good and unaffected.

**A swap no longer requires a verdict.** `TrackSwap` refused any unjudged track — "there is no
verdict to carry across" — which refused exactly the tracks this creates, since a shortfall stops
before the verdict. The restatement is now skipped when there is no run to restate, which is what
it was always for, and the plan says which of the two is about to happen. This was not anticipated
by #23 and was found by reading `PlanFor` rather than by running it.

**Nothing recorded reads as no finding.** Every working set already on disk predates the record,
and none of them park.

**An unreadable `premiumStatus` reads as `Unreported`.** A StemForge that names a new outcome must
not park every track, nor throw while recording a download that actually succeeded.

## What was measured, and when

All of this was re-measured 2026-09-10 before building, against a live instance rather than the
issue body:

- `AppSettings.YtdlpCookiesFromBrowser` is `"firefox"`, so the premium expectation is held and the
  signal is live. Were it ever cleared, every download would return `NotApplicable` and nothing
  would park — correctly, because nothing could then be said.
- `dQw4w9WgXcQ` carries no marker and resolves format 141 at 257.5 kbps, `isPremium: true`,
  auto-selected, `premiumShortfall: false`. The 42% case, still true.
- The acquisition fields are populated on the **success path only**: a failed input constructs its
  result with the first four arguments and nulls the rest.
- The enum is `PremiumStatus`; `PremiumExpectation` is the evaluator class. #23's body named the
  latter and listed five of its seven members, omitting `NotApplicable` and `Premium`.
